thread_focus: whether a call `lockInGuess(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: lockInGuess(h) from a fresh account with exactly 1 ether sent always succeeds, stores h and sets the settle-eligibility block to the next block, so settle() immediately reverts while the new guess exists.

thread_focus: whether a call `lockInGuess(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: lockInGuess reverts when the caller already has an active guess, leaving the stored guess unchanged.

thread_focus: whether a call `lockInGuess(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: lockInGuess must accept exactly 1 ether and revert if the sender sends any other value or already has an active guess.

thread_focus: whether a call `lockInGuess(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: A lockInGuess call with any value other than exactly 1 ether always reverts, so an improperly funded attempt cannot create a new active guess.

thread_focus: whether a call `lockInGuess(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: An attempt to lock in a guess through lockInGuess succeeds exactly when the caller sends exactly 1 ether AND does not already have an active guess, and its success or failure is independent of the guess hash value provided; in particular, sending exactly 1 ether with a previously used account cannot create a second active guess.

thread_focus: whether a call `settle(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: A settle() call by the same sender can only succeed if that sender first lockInGuess() with 1 ether, and before settling the locked-in guess must still be pending (not settled), after which settle() either pays 2 ether or not depending on the guess.

thread_focus: whether a call `settle(args)` reverts or completes, and on which inputs
property_summary: A settle() call by a sender who has no pending scheduled guess (i.e., guesses[msg.sender].block was never set or is already 0 after settling) must always revert, since settling requires guesses[msg.sender].block != 0.
